title: Telling stories & real conversation
goal: Tell a story, link sentences with 'who / where / when', report what people said, and sound natural with fillers and idioms.
intro: Congratulations — you've reached the last unit! Now it's time to sound less like a textbook and more like a person. You'll learn how Hindi speakers tell stories, the little words that fill real conversation (**मतलब**, **वैसे**, **यार**, **है ना?**), a handful of much-loved idioms, and two structures that let you build longer sentences: **relative clauses** (जो… वह…) and **reported speech** (उसने कहा कि…).

vocab.en: to tell (a story), recite; to make hear

vocab.note: m · pl unchanged · also one's home town: मेरा गाँव
m · पुराने ज़माने में 'in the old days'
oblique: जिस (sg), जिन (pl) · जिसने, जिन्होंने, जिसका
f · X की वजह से 'because of X'
X के बिना or बिना X के
m · बीच में 'in the middle; meanwhile'; X के बीच 'between X'
Very common conversation opener: वैसे… 'by the way…'
Informal, very common among friends of any gender: अरे यार!
ऐसी, ऐसे · वैसा 'like that'; कैसा 'what like?'

phrases.en: Once upon a time… / This one time…
By the way, where are you from?
This is the limit! / That's too much!
Stop pestering me! (lit. don't eat my brain)
Don't lose heart. (lit. don't make your heart small)
A bad workman blames his tools. (lit. can't dance, says the courtyard is crooked)
The grass is always greener. (lit. distant drums sound sweet)
A drop in the ocean. (lit. a cumin seed in a camel's mouth)
Everyone has a different opinion. (lit. as many mouths, so many words)

grammar.title: Relative clauses: जो … वह …
grammar.body:
English puts 'who/which' clauses inside the sentence (*the boy **who is standing there** is my brother*). Hindi usually uses a **pair** of words: a **j-** word in the relative clause and a matching **v-/t-** word in the main clause:

**जो** लड़का वहाँ खड़ा है, **वह** मेरा भाई है 'The boy who is standing there is my brother' (lit. 'which boy is standing there, he is my brother').

The j-word changes like any pronoun: oblique **जिस** (sg) / **जिन** (pl): **जिस** दुकान से मैंने यह लिया… 'the shop I bought this from…'; with ने: **जिसने**, **जिन्होंने**; possessive **जिसका**.

Other pairs follow the same logic:
**जहाँ … वहाँ** where … there · **जब … तब** when … then
**जैसा … वैसा** as … so · **जितना … उतना** as much … that much

In speech the main-clause word is often dropped, and the clause can also follow: वह आदमी, **जो** कल आया था…

examples.native: जो किताब मेज़ पर है, वह मेरी है।
examples.roman: jo kitāb mez par hai, vah merī hai.
examples.en: The book that's on the table is mine.

examples.native: जिस आदमी ने मेरी मदद की, वह डॉक्टर था।
examples.roman: jis ādmī ne merī madad kī, vah ḍokṭar thā.
examples.en: The man who helped me was a doctor.

examples.native: जहाँ मैं रहता हूँ, वहाँ बहुत शोर है।
examples.roman: jahāṃ maiṃ rahtā hūṃ, vahāṃ bahut shor hai.
examples.en: Where I live, it's very noisy.

examples.native: जब मैं छोटा था, तब हम गाँव में रहते थे।
examples.roman: jab maiṃ chhoṭā thā, tab ham gāṃv meṃ rahte the.
examples.en: When I was small, we lived in a village.
The more you study, the more you'll learn.

grammar.title: Reporting speech: उसने कहा कि…
grammar.body:
Hindi reporting is simpler than English: after **कहा कि / बताया कि / पूछा कि**, you usually keep the **original tense**, and often even the original words:

Ravi: 'मैं कल आऊँगा।' → **रवि ने कहा कि वह कल आएगा** 'Ravi said that he would come tomorrow' (tense stays future).

Very often speakers simply quote directly: **रवि ने कहा, "मैं कल आऊँगा।"** — and in casual speech, even without changing मैं: रवि बोला कि मैं कल आऊँगा (context makes it clear).

**Questions**: पूछा कि **क्या** … (for yes/no), or keep the question word: उसने पूछा कि तुम कहाँ रहते हो.
**Requests/commands**: कहा कि + **subjunctive**: माँ ने कहा कि मैं जल्दी घर आऊँ 'Mum told me to come home early'.

In speech **बोलना** often replaces कहना, and **बोला / बोली** take no ने: वह बोली कि… 'she said that…'.

examples.native: उसने कहा कि वह बीमार है।
examples.roman: usne kahā ki vah bīmār hai.

examples.native: दुकानदार ने बताया कि दुकान सात बजे बंद होती है।
examples.roman: dukāndār ne batāyā ki dukān sāt baje band hotī hai.
examples.en: The shopkeeper told me the shop closes at seven.

examples.native: उन्होंने पूछा कि क्या मैं हिंदी समझती हूँ।
examples.roman: unhoṃne pūchhā ki kyā maiṃ hindī samajhtī hūṃ.
examples.en: He/she asked whether I understood Hindi. (woman speaking)

examples.native: डॉक्टर ने कहा कि मैं आराम करूँ।
examples.roman: ḍokṭar ne kahā ki maiṃ ārām karūṃ.
examples.en: The doctor told me to rest.

grammar.title: Sounding natural: storytelling words and fillers
grammar.body:
**Telling a story**: एक बार की बात है… 'one time…' → पहले 'first' → फिर / उसके बाद 'then / after that' → अचानक 'suddenly' → तभी 'just then' → आख़िरकार 'finally'.

**Fillers and tags** that make you sound fluent:
**है ना?** / **ना?** — 'isn't it? right?' (tag question): अच्छा है, है ना?
**मतलब…** / **यानी…** — 'I mean… / that is…'
**वैसे…** — 'by the way… / actually…'
**अच्छा…** — 'OK… / I see… / oh really?'
**हाँ तो…** — 'so, anyway…' (getting back to the story)
**ख़ैर…** — 'anyway…' (moving on)
**यार** — 'mate' (friends only)
**क्या बोलते हैं…** — 'what do you call it…' (while searching for a word)

**Emphasis particles**: **ही** 'only, exactly' (मैं ही 'I myself', आज ही 'this very day'), **भी** 'also, even', **तो** 'as for…' (मैं तो थक गया 'as for me, I'm exhausted').

examples.native: एक बार की बात है, एक गाँव में एक बूढ़ा किसान रहता था।
examples.roman: ek bār kī bāt hai, ek gāṃv meṃ ek būṛhā kisān rahtā thā.
examples.en: Once upon a time, an old farmer lived in a village.
Just then, suddenly the power went out.

examples.native: मतलब, मुझे पक्का नहीं पता, लेकिन…
examples.roman: matlab, mujhe pakkā nahīṃ patā, lekin…
examples.en: I mean, I don't know for sure, but…

examples.native: हाँ तो, मैं क्या कह रहा था?
examples.roman: hāṃ to, maiṃ kyā kah rahā thā?
examples.en: So, anyway, what was I saying?

dialogue.title: The wedding story
dialogue.setting: Aisha meets her friend Ravi, who has just come back from his cousin's wedding in a village near Jaipur.

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.native: अरे रवि! तुम वापस आ गए? शादी कैसी रही?
lines.roman: are Ravi! tum vāpas ā gaye? shādī kaisī rahī?
lines.en: Hey Ravi! You're back? How was the wedding?

lines.speaker: Ravi
lines.native: यार, क्या बताऊँ! बहुत मज़ा आया, पर एक मज़ेदार बात भी हुई।
lines.roman: yār, kyā batāūṃ! bahut mazā āyā, par ek mazedār bāt bhī huī.
lines.en: Oh man, where do I start! It was great fun, but something funny happened too.

lines.speaker: Ravi
lines.native: हुआ यह कि बारात शाम को निकलने वाली थी। दूल्हा घोड़ी पर बैठा था, बैंड बज रहा था…
lines.roman: huā yah ki bārāt shām ko nikalne vālī thī. dūlhā ghoṛī par baiṭhā thā, baiṇḍ baj rahā thā…
lines.en: What happened was, the wedding procession was about to set off in the evening. The groom was sitting on the mare, the band was playing…

lines.speaker: Ravi
lines.native: तभी अचानक घोड़ी डर गई और भागने लगी — दूल्हे के साथ!
lines.roman: tabhī achānak ghoṛī ḍar gaī aur bhāgne lagī — dūlhe ke sāth!
lines.en: Just then the mare suddenly got scared and started running — with the groom on her!

lines.speaker: Ravi
lines.native: जो लड़का घोड़ी की देखभाल करता था, वह उसके पीछे दौड़ा। पूरा गाँव हँस रहा था!
lines.roman: jo laṛkā ghoṛī kī dekhbhāl kartā thā, vah uske pīchhe dauṛā. pūrā gāṃv haṃs rahā thā!
lines.en: The boy who looked after the mare ran after her. The whole village was laughing!

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.native: बेचारा दूल्हा! वह ठीक तो था, ना?
lines.roman: bechārā dūlhā! vah ṭhīk to thā, nā?
lines.en: Poor groom! He was OK, right?

lines.speaker: Ravi
lines.native: हाँ, आख़िरकार घोड़ी रुक गई। दूल्हे ने कहा कि अगली बार वह गाड़ी से आएगा!
lines.roman: hāṃ, āxirkār ghoṛī ruk gaī. dūlhe ne kahā ki aglī bār vah gāṛī se āyegā!
lines.en: Yes, in the end the mare stopped. The groom said next time he'll come by car!

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.native: अगली बार? हा हा! वैसे, दुल्हन ने क्या कहा?
lines.roman: aglī bār? hā hā! vaise, dulhan ne kyā kahā?
lines.en: Next time? Ha ha! By the way, what did the bride say?

lines.speaker: Ravi
lines.native: वह बोली, "चलता है — कम से कम वह भागा तो नहीं!"
lines.roman: vah bolī, "chaltā hai — kam se kam vah bhāgā to nahīṃ!"
lines.en: She said, "Never mind — at least he didn't run away!"

culture: Real-life Hindi is full of **code-switching**: urban speakers slide between Hindi and English mid-sentence ('Hinglish' — मैं literally shocked हो गया!), and it's perfectly normal. Hindi is also rich in **idioms and proverbs** (मुहावरे and कहावतें), often about animals, food and village life; dropping one into conversation always gets a smile. Storytelling is a cherished tradition, from grandmothers' tales (दादी-नानी की कहानियाँ) to the epic Ramayana and Mahabharata. From here, the best next steps are Hindi films and songs with Hindi subtitles, podcasts, and — most of all — talking to people. **आपकी हिंदी की यात्रा के लिए शुभकामनाएँ!** Best wishes for your Hindi journey!
